title: pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTSDReader
body:
## pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTSDReader

Reads FVCOM (Finite-Volume Community Ocean Model) netCDF output on an unstructured triangular grid with sigma layers and levels where one file holds many time records. Use pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTMDReader for multi-domain master files and pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_STSDReader for one time per file. If the output follows the UGRID conventions, the native pvNetCDFUGRIDreader is an alternative. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Variables live on different meshes (nodes, elements, layers, levels); select the mesh that carries each array you need.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTSDReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTSDReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from FVCOM data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The FVCOM plugin offers the ocean fields (velocity, temperature, salinity, elevation, …) of the output; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single FVCOM file to read (.nc, .cdf, .elev, .ncd); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The FVCOM plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the FVCOM meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The FVCOM plugin reports the 2-D grid and the sigma-layer and sigma-level meshes. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from FVCOM data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The FVCOM plugin offers the ocean fields (velocity, temperature, salinity, elevation, …) of the output; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTSDReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
